title: The Five Competitive Forces That Shape Strategy (Michael E. Porter, January 2008)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Competition is wider than direct rivals: customers, suppliers, potential entrants and substitutes, together with rivals, set an industry's structure and profit potential.

title: Know Your Customers' "Jobs to Be Done" (Christensen, Hall, Dillon and Duncan, September 2016)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Innovation is less of a gamble when firms understand the job customers are trying to get done, rather than product features or the customer data they already hold.

title: Rediscovering Market Segmentation (Daniel Yankelovich and David Meer, February 2006)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Segmentation had narrowed into psychographic profiling for advertising; its real purpose is to find customers whose behaviour can be changed or whose needs are unmet, using what predicts buying.

title: The Mom Test (Rob Fitzpatrick)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The author's page for the book: a practical guide to getting honest learning from customer conversations when people are being polite rather than truthful, and to judging whether a prospect will actually buy.

title: ICC/ESOMAR International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics (updated July 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF text extracted). Five fundamental principles; Art. 1 duty of care and keeping research apart from non-research activity with separate consent; Art. 2 children; Art. 3 data minimisation; Art. 4 primary data collection, including notifying a synthetic persona at the start; Art. 5 secondary data; Art. 6 deductive disclosure; Art. 7 fit for purpose, telling clients when AI or synthetic data is used and the extent of human oversight; Art. 9 publishing findings.

title: MRS Code of Conduct (2023)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 2023 Code came into effect on 15 May 2023 and applied to all members and company partners from 14 August 2023; changes include more focus on participant wellbeing and clearer reporting of representative samples such as "Nat Rep" with the sampling parameters used.

title: Code of Standards and Ethics for Market Research and Data Analytics (updated September 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Research kept separate from advertising and direct marketing; tell participants at the start if an AI chatbot or avatar collecting data could be mistaken for a human; disclose AI tools used; distinguish synthetic or AI-generated data from data from real people; extra care and verifiable consent for children.

title: IA's Code In Action: Synthetic Participants in Market Research (Scott Swigart, 16 September 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Synthetic participants are AI models built on real research data; use should be fully disclosed with their limits and method; anonymise data before it goes to an AI; the author calls them experimental.

title: AAPOR Code: Disclosure Standards
publisher: American Association for Public Opinion Research
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Items to disclose: sponsor and who conducted the work, question wording, population, sample design (probability or not, frame, quotas, incentives), mode, dates, sample sizes and precision, weighting, quality checks and limitations; margin of error for probability samples; precision for non-probability samples only with the model and assumptions explained.

title: Writing Survey Questions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Open versus closed questions; question order effects; agree-disagree items invite acquiescence bias and forced choices are preferred; avoid double-barrelled questions; response order effects and randomising unordered lists; pretesting with pilots and cognitive interviews.

title: Online opt-in polls can produce misleading results, especially for young people and Hispanic adults (5 March 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Bogus respondents in opt-in samples inflate rare attitudes and behaviours; in a February 2022 test 12% of opt-in adults under 30 claimed a licence to operate a nuclear submarine, a share that rounds to 0% in reality; probability panels showed very few such answers.

title: Understanding the margin of error in election polls (8 September 2016)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A simple random sample of 1,067 gives about plus or minus 3 points at 95% confidence; weighted polls have larger margins; subgroups have much larger margins; the margin on a difference is roughly twice as large; the margin covers sampling error only.

title: Sample sizes for saturation in qualitative research: A systematic review of empirical tests (Hennink and Kaiser, Social Science & Medicine, 2022)
supports: Fetch blocked by a cookie wall; confirmed by a WebSearch result showing this exact page. 23 articles reviewed; studies reached saturation within 9 to 17 interviews or 4 to 8 focus groups, particularly with relatively homogeneous populations and narrowly defined objectives; Soc Sci Med 2022;292:114523.

title: Van Westendorp Pricing Sensitivity Meter (blog post)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Developed by Peter van Westendorp in the 1970s; four price questions (too cheap, a bargain, getting expensive, too expensive); range read from crossing cumulative curves; limits: ignores competitive context, does not predict volume, weak theory behind the crossing points; the Newton-Miller-Smith extension (1993) adds purchase intent.

title: The top reasons startups fail (5 March 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Post-mortems of 431 VC-backed companies that shut down since 2023, with reasons found for 385; 70% ran out of cash (usually the final cause, not the root); 43% poor product-market fit; reasons overlap.

title: County Business Patterns (CBP)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page revised 5 August 2026). Annual data on establishments with paid employees by NAICS industry and geography: establishments, employment in the week of 12 March, first-quarter and annual payroll; latest data year 2023.

title: Nonemployer Statistics (NES)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page revised 29 September 2026). Annual counts and receipts of US businesses with no paid employees, by industry and geography; latest data year 2024.

title: Consumer Expenditure Surveys
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The only federal household survey covering the full range of consumer spending and income; 2025 annual release dated 29 October 2026 reports average consumer unit spending of $81,905, up 4.3% on 2024; tables by demographics and geography.

title: American Community Survey (ACS)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Ongoing household survey since 2005 covering more than 40 topics (income, housing, employment, commuting); 2025 1-year estimates released in late October 2026; 2020-2024 5-year files available.

title: Family spending in the UK: April 2024 to March 2025 (released 11 June 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Average weekly household spending was 676.60 pounds in the year ending March 2025, a nominal rise of 53.30 pounds (9%); based on the Living Costs and Food Survey; figures are means.

title: Structural business statistics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. EU statistics on the structure, activity and performance of businesses by NACE activity, with good coverage across enterprise size classes; a 30 September 2026 news item reported EU business value added for 2024.

title: Country Commercial Guides
publisher: International Trade Administration (US Department of Commerce)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Reports on a country's market conditions, opportunities, regulations and business customs, prepared by US embassy staff from Commerce, State and other agencies.

title: Access2Markets
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Commission's trade portal: My Trade Assistant for the conditions to trade a product (including rules of origin), EU trade agreements and statistics, a single entry point to report trade barriers, and an SME corner for exporters.

title: Market guides
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Country-by-country export guides covering doing business, tax rates and import regulations, filterable by sector, region or trading bloc; www.great.gov.uk/markets/ now redirects here (HTTP 301 seen when checked).

title: Data protection explained
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The GDPR principles organisations must follow when processing personal data: lawfulness, fairness and transparency; purpose limitation; data minimisation; accuracy; storage limitation; integrity and confidentiality; accountability.

title: Trade secrets
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Directive (EU) 2016/943 protects confidential business information against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure, with civil remedies; reverse engineering and parallel innovation stay lawful; acquisition by illicit means such as unauthorised access or breach of contract is unlawful.

title: Business Guide to the FTC's Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Sellers need a reasonable basis for any shipping time; with no time stated, ship within 30 days (50 for credit applications); delays require an option to cancel for a prompt refund; dry-testing products not yet available is allowed only under specific conditions, such as disclosing that the product is planned and not implying shipment.

title: Providing clear and accurate information about prices: summary (CMA209, updated 7 January 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Mandatory fees and taxes belong in the headline price; drip pricing is described as illegal, with penalties up to 10% of turnover or 300,000 pounds, whichever is greater; optional extras may be shown separately but clearly.

title: The Fair Housing Act (updated 22 June 2023)
publisher: US Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Act bars housing discrimination based on race or colour, religion, sex, national origin, familial status and disability; it covers steering home seekers to areas based on race and giving false information about availability.
